market_question: US x Iran permanent peace deal by June 30, 2026?
reasoning: A permanent peace accord ending military hostilities between the US and Iran by mid-2026 is virtually impossible given the 45‑year adversarial relationship, the absence of any precedent, and the high bar set by the resolution criteria. The market description’s reference to a temporary ceasefire in April 2026 suggests a recent escalation, not a path to a definitive peace deal. Even the JCPOA never constituted a peace agreement, making the notion of a full permanent peace deal by that date extraordinarily unlikely.
evidence_points: No U.S.-Iran peace agreement has ever been established since the 1979 revolution; formal diplomatic ties remain severed.
The 2015 nuclear deal (JCPOA) did not include language ending military hostilities, and that agreement was significantly less ambitious than a permanent peace deal.
The market’s own hypothetical scenario includes a temporary ceasefire in April 2026, implying recent conflict and making immediate and permanent resolution implausible.
sources_consulted: Historical record of US-Iran relations since 1979
Analysis of the JCPOA and its limitations
